newsitem.title: USA: Strong hiring intentions seen in Q3, Manpower says.
newsitem.headline: Strong hiring intentions seen in Q3, Manpower says.

text.p: The inability of some companies to find employees they needed earlier this year is leading to the strongest third-quarter hiring plans since 1988, according to a survey from the temporary help firm Manpower Inc.

"Much of the present demand is for seasonal workers in such industries as construction and services, but the need for workers is so widespread that there seems to be a carryover demand caused by the inability of companies to find the people they needed in earlier quarters," Mitchell Fromstein, Manpower's chief executive, said in a news release.

Of the more than 16,000 companies surveyed, 30 percent said they will be searching for additional workers in the third quarter, up from 28 percent in the previous quarter and 27 percent last year, Manpower said.
"A very unusual combination of factors is at work in the labour market, underlying the strongest third-quarter hiring intentions since 1988," Fromstein said.
Five percent of those surveyed expect staff cutbacks, 61 percent expect no change and 4 percent are not certain yet, Manpower said.

Last quarter 6 percent said they planned cutbacks, 63 percent expected to remain at current levels and 3 percent were unsure. A year ago, 7 percent anticipated cutbacks, 63 percent saw no change and 3 percent were uncertain, Milwaukee-based Manpower said.
Fromstein said that all regions of the country expressed hiring intentions not surpassed since 1988-89, but that the job outlook was particularly bright in the Midwest.

In the construction industry, 40 percent plan to hire more workers while just four percent expect to trim down. In durable goods manufacturing, 34 percent intend to increase recruiting and 6 percent will decrease employment, while in non-durable goods manufacturing, 27 percent plan to increase staff and 6 percent plan declines.
In transportation and public utilities, 24 percent expect to hire and 5 percent plan to cut staffing, while in wholesale and retail trades 34 percent plan to add staff, while 4 percent plan to cut.
The demand in wholesale and retail trades is the highest seen since 1978, except for fourth-quarter holiday hiring, Manpower said.

In finance, insurance and real estate, 22 percent expect to add workers and 5 percent expect to cut back, Manpower said. In education, 22 percent plan recruiting, while 10 percent plan lower staffing.
Twenty-eight percent of service firms plan hiring and 5 percent plan cutbacks, while in public administration, 28 percent plan to add workers and 5 percent plan to trim down, Manpower said.
The survey is based on telephone interviews in 487 U.S. cities and has a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percent.
